reason: Since #987 auto-admission started a project worker only for an open chat or a chat-start command, so every other project-routed write (rename, archive, delete and anything else the API delivers to the project's worker) on a project without an open chat stayed queued with 202 forever; archived projects were skipped outright, so deleting one could never run, and the stranded rows blocked runtime-stop. Queued non-barrier project commands now admit exactly their project (archived included, retirement-held excluded); idle retirement waits for queued or running project commands and request_project_retirement declines while one is queued; a request arriving during a retirement hold waits (bounded) and is then admitted instead of a 409. Selection covers chatless edit and archived delete through real API ingress, routing and auto-admission; retirement declining with queued work and ignoring host-committed barriers; the bounded ingress wait and its 409 bound; the existing chat-scoped admission, child/parent, legacy goal-create, metadata-batch and read no-admission cases; retirement hold and release contracts (the #987 hold test now records that retirement declines while project commands are queued); readmission fence and held-project cases; and the API worker suite for the changed ingress.
exclusions: No UI, native or frontend code changed, so no frontend, native or Playwright tests; the operator journey (empty project rename, archive and delete through the API and the desktop project switcher, delete right after the last chat, runtime-stop afterwards) was checked on scratch supervisor Cores (see the PR). test_runtime_reconciliation.py, test_runtime_chat_resume.py, test_runtime_chat_stream.py and the real-Core test in test_shutdown_readmission.py fail identically on main in this environment (pidfd, fixture and LAN prerequisites); across the 13 related files no test fails only with this change. PostgreSQL parametrizations are collected but skip in CI; they pass locally on PostgreSQL 16. No live or staging Core mutation, database backup, or deployment.
